missing_required_content: Brief section 8 per-dimension grading is absent. Section 8 requires each shortlisted workflow to be classified strong / moderate / weak / negative / unknown on 17 dimensions (annual volume, human review rate, H share, cost per review, cost of wrong decision, recurrence of settlements, codifiability, decision owner, structured evidence, integration complexity, regulatory constraints, incumbent strength, buyer, willingness to pay, sales cycle, initial ACV, expansion potential). Table B carries only the seven section-10B columns plus one overall evidence grade; integration complexity, regulatory constraints, willingness to pay, sales cycle, ACV and expansion potential are never graded for any of the eight rows.

Brief section 4 quantification items 'addressable user count' and 'software spend' are not stated per workflow, not even as 'unknown'. F item 9 covers pricing and ACV but no row or gap entry says the addressable user count is unknown.

Brief section 5 asks for an A-to-H split per use case. Several Table B rows give partial splits: the EBA reporting row gives no A-to-H split at all (54% template interpretation is a regulator-level C share, not a review split); the KYC row gives only C, H and A; the mortgage row omits D, E, F, G; the P&C row omits C through G. Each row should either complete the split or state 'remaining categories not estimated'.

The draft repeatedly relies on documents that are not in the digest, the cluster files or its own source key: 'the three deep dives on those pools, after refutation', 'corrected by the refuter', 'the reviewer-repaired design', 'the refuter struck the earlier use of that corpus'. Section 10 and the evidence-limitation paragraph require every load-bearing input to be traceable; the report must name those files with paths in the source key or drop the claims that rest on them (notably the C1 CROSS statistics that appear nowhere in tax-customs-export-controls.json, which I could reproduce from the CSV but a reader cannot trace).

Section 10C 'how often the same class recurs' for C2 is answered with an IPSA analogy (93% at coarse class, 37% at fine class). IPSA classes are purchase classes, not ambiguity classes (falsification verifier), and expenses are a different domain; the field should read 'unknown, no analogue transfers' rather than borrow a number.

The geography requirement (distinguish US, EU and French conditions where regulation matters) is met only by [RECALL] statements. The report should say in one line that no EU or French review pool or regulator primary was read beyond three GitHub mirrors (EBA Q&A, OpenFisca-France, Code du travail numerique), so every EU and French statement outside those is recall.

A self-constructed proxy described as a measurement of the target quantity. H2 row and C1 Recurrence call the same-day clusters of rulings citing one precedent 'cross-product recurrence of one interpretive question' at '1 to 2% of public rulings'. Same-day co-citation mostly captures batch filings by one requester on one day (for example N341630 to N341634 on 2024-08-20, all citing 556449), which is the opposite of an interpretive question recurring over time. The count is also definition-sensitive: grouping by (date, cited ruling) over the CSV gives 49 groups / 135 rulings at two or more and 22 / 81 at three or more (3.4% and 2.0% of 3,971), against the draft's 28 / 75 and 11 / 41.

Non-reproducible arithmetic on an unsourced model. C2 ROI: 100,000 applications, 15% manual review, 10% escalation gives 1,500 escalations; an H pool of 150 to 300 implies 10 to 20% H, but Table B gives H 5 to 10%; and 150 to 300 cases at 75 USD is 11,250 to 22,500 USD, not 9,000 to 16,500 USD.

factual_errors_vs_evidence: Stripe requirement error codes (verified against https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/openapi/master/openapi/spec3.json, account_requirements_error.code, 96 values). The draft's partition 30 document + 17 URL + 23 identity + 19 format + 5 denylists + 3 other sums to 97 because invalid_url_denylisted is counted twice. Correct partition: 30 verification_document_*, 16 invalid_url_* excluding the denylisted one, 23 verification_* identity/ownership/tax-id, 19 other invalid_* format and value codes, 5 *_denylisted, 3 other (external_request, information_missing, unsupported_business_type). '91 of 96 are evidence, identity or format' is 96 minus the 5 denylists, not the 88 that those three categories actually contain. More important, this enum is the requirements-verification (KYC data) vocabulary; restricted-business outcomes are expressed in disabled_reason (rejected.listed, rejected.terms_of_service; capability-level rejected.unsupported_business), so 'none names a restricted-business category decision' is true by construction and cannot inform the review split.

verdict: Revise before release. The draft meets the shape of brief section 10 (A through H, all twelve C sub-fields for three workflows, eight H categories with economic gates, the prescribed closing sentence) and its direction, evidence against a standalone product, is consistent with the verified record. Its GitHub-sourced citations largely reproduce from the primaries: I recomputed the CROSS statistics from the 216,164-row scrape, confirmed the Avalara field names at commit 23416f6, every HMRC enum and the 'valid from {0} to {1}' string, the Adyen enums, HMDA fields 96 to 107, the Stripe business_type and structure counts, the EBA mortgage counts (103, 1, and 3/3/2), the Ballerine quotes and version fields, the vladswork accuracy table and the Orlando corpus counts. Five defects require correction before the report can stand: (1) the executive answer and closing sentence present estimates as measurements of H, contradicting the draft's own limitation paragraph and H1/H2 rows; (2) the Stripe error-code partition double-counts one code, its '91 of 96' does not follow from its categories, and the enum is the wrong object for the claim it supports; (3) C1 contains a logic error ('four reasons, only one of them H' with none being H) and misfiles chapter 99 as interpretation against the source it cites; (4) the section 8 per-dimension grading is missing and several A-to-H splits are incomplete; (5) the report leans on deep-dive, refuter and reviewer documents absent from the digest, the cluster files and its source key, and it reuses its own modelled labour figures as evidence for H8. Secondary fixes: relabel AHIP, Ballerine and Avalara material as industry or vendor claims; drop the IPSA recurrence analogy from C2 and the HMRC referral vocabulary from the importer row; correct the PubLedge over-read; state CROSS definitions so the three statistics that wobble on recomputation (85 versus 87 lines, median 39 versus 32, 2023 HQ 27 versus 26) are explained.
